newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 31.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
PAY PANEL RAISES RETIREMENT AGE, CUTS HOLIDAYS

The fifth pay commission recommended raising the retirement age to 60 years, increasing house rent allowance and a minimum salary of 2,440 rupees. In its report submitted to the government, the panel recommended a maximum salary of 26,000 rupees per month, a drastic cut in holidays to three days a year from the present 17 alongwith a six day working week. It also recommended enhancing the maximum recruitment age of women to 35 years, a 15 day paternity leave and transport allowances for all employees. The commission also suggested a freeze on further employment of junior staff and a sharp cut back in intake for higher levels. It also recommended employment on contract basis in the govern
The Hindustan Times
SPECIAL TEAM TO PROBE BOFORS DEAL

A special investigation team (SIT) was constituted by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to look into all aspects of the Bofors case. An additional director would lead the team consisting of other senior officials of the investigating agency. The SIT was appointed to facilitate fast investigation into the case and the team planned to wrap up investigations without delay. Besides going through the 500-page document which arrived in India from the Swiss authorities in the previous week, all other aspects of the case would be probed by the team which would be supervised by the CBI chief himself. Sources said the help of Interpol might also be sought in the case.
The Economic Times
INDIA AMONG WORLD'S TOP FISH PRODUCERS

India emerged as the world's second largest producer of inland fish and the seventh largest producer of all fish, including marine catch in 1995/96 (April-March). This was despite the environmental crises in shrimp farms and the continuing turf war between traditional farmers and mechanised trawler boats. Exports of marine products rose 800 percent since 1984/85, from 3.84 billion rupees 35.01 billion in 1995/96. Of this, 67 percent came from shrimp farming. However, following the Supreme Court ban on intensive aquaculture farms on environmental grounds, exports for 1997 were expected to suffer heavy losses.
STATE FIRMS ALLOWED TO INVEST IN UNIT TRUST FUNDS

State-owned firms (PSUs) were allowed to invest their surplus funds in Unit Trust of India's (UTI) mutual funds. This was likely to inject considerable short-term liquidity in the stock market as UTI was the largest domestic institutional player in the market. The PSUs' short-term surplus funds could earlier be placed with banks as part of portfolio management schemes. But after being misused during the securities scam in 1992, the government had banned placement of PSU surplus funds in the market. Subsequently the Finance Ministry had eased the norms for deployment of such funds with banks as certificate of deposits (CDs). Presently, banks, flush with funds, were not attracting CDs from
CORPORATISATION OF PORTS ON THE ANVIL

Corporatisation of the 11 major ports is on the agenda of the Surface Transport Ministry. This comes close on the heels of the announcement of port guidelines for private investment. The ministry had earlier opened the road and the port sectors for private investment. The move to corporatise ports was in line with the ministry's perception that there was an urgent need to give more autonomy to the ports in order to effect improvement in their efficiency and also to have speedier modernisation programmes at the ports. According to the India Infrastructure Report a 100 billion rupee investment was required at the 11 major ports during 1997/2001.
Financial Express
20 BLN RUPEE FOREIGN INVESTMENT OFFERS APPROVED

The Industry Minister approved 142 foreign direct investment (FDI) proposals boasting of a 50 billion rupee export potential. The proposals include those of Bombay Dyeing, RPG Paging, Schuler GmbH and Fred Schemetz Gmbh, Germany and are worth 20 billion rupees. Approvals were given in electronics, agri-business, infrastructure, engineering, health and mining services. Korea's IG Electronic was allowed a 100 percent subsidiary unit for manufacturing electronic and electrical appliances with a total FDI of 20.475 billion rupees. Two proposals by Matushita Electric for making air conditioners and washing machines was also cleared involving a total FDI of about 490 million rupees. Among othe
STATES LEFT OUT OF REFORMS PROCESS

The federal government has failed to involve the states in the process of economic reforms. This was stated by the India Development Report 1997, released by the central bank governor. The report summarises India's economic situation at the beginning of 1997. The independent assessment of the situation was taken up in the last quarter of 1996, when the shadow of an impending recession loomed large over the country. On the imposition of the minimum alternate tax (MAT), the report stated MAT was not the best way to tackle tax evasion. MAT generated incentives for companies to indulge in window dressing and creative accounting to show low profits to reduce investments and pay higher dividen
STOCK LENDING SCHEME APPROVED

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) approved the introduction of a stock lending scheme. The scheme revolves around intermediaries who would function as banks to securities deposited with them. SEBI also agreed to review the guidelines on primary market allotment to give preference to small investors who apply for 2OO shares in an issue. On the mutual fund front, the regulator allowed schemes for fixed income securities to mention an indicative return, apart from the existing permission to offer assured returns. The revised guidelines would be announced soon.
FINANCIAL SECTOR UNIONS TO COME TOGETHER

Bank trade unions, bank officers associations and employees associations in financial institutions decided to get together to forge a common programme. This is the first time that employees of the entire financial sector decided to come together to solve issues which have been irritants to some or all of them. Employees' unions of insurance companies also agreed to participate. Presently, insurance and bank employees are fighting against privatisation. While the banking sector is flooded with private operators, the insurance sector is yet to be opened up to the private sector.
Business Standard
TELECOMMUNICATION PROJECTS GET INFRASTRUCTURE STATUS

Telecommunication projects have been designated as infrastructure investments. The government also raised the ceiling on external commercial borrowings (ECB) in the sector from 35 to 50 percent of project cost. However, no decision was taken on tax deductibility of licence fees. Licence fees paid by the state-owned telecommunication firms are treated as revenue expenditure. The immediate benefit of the new categorisation was a 50 percent reduction in project import duties, from 52 to 25 percent. Another benefit would be the five-year tax holiday and concessional tax rates for the remaining period of the project life.
DCM TO RAISE 1.5 BLN RUPEES FROM REAL ESTATE, STAKE SELLOFF

DCM would raise 1.5 billion rupees from the sale of its stake in its automobile venture with Daewoo and sale of real estate. The Vinay Bharat Ram-controlled group received 517 million rupees from the divestment of its 24 percent stake in DCM Daewoo and expects to raise another one billion rupees from sale of real estate by the year-end. The cash-strapped company would use the proceeds to reduce its debt and plans to bring down its current debt-equity ratio from the existing 2.7:1 to 2:1. The group was now focussing on becoming a leading player in the engineering goods industry and funds generated from the real estate business would be invested to strengthen the engineering business. FOREIGN INSTITUTIONS CAN INVEST IN GILTS

The bourse regulator (SEBI) has allowed foreign institutional investors (FIIs) to invest in dated government securities. This would be within the framework of guidelines on FII investment in 100 percent debt funds. Investment in gilts would be subject to an annual cap within the overall external commercial borrowing limit. The government and the central bank have already given their approval for such investments. SEBI also decided to allow FII owned proprietary funds that are regulated by their home regulators or are registered with their tax authorities. The regulator will also do away with the regulation pertaining to the need to have broad-based funds. This was expected to facilitate
COURT PUTS MOST DISTILLERIES UNDER STATE CONTROL

The Supreme Court has ruled that the federal government would levy duties and exercise total and exclusive control on industries manufacturing rectified spirit meant exclusively for supply to industries. However, manufacturers of rectified spirit for use as potable liquors would be under total and exclusive control of state governments in all respects and at all stages. This would also include the establishment of the distillery. With most distilleries falling under the potable category, the ruling has come as a boon for state governments. Apart from earning revenue from distilleries by way of taxes, states would also have total control over them from the point of establishment.
The Observer
LEFT PARTY SPELLS STAND ON BROADCAST BILL

The Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPM) opposed the government's move to allow foreign participation in the media through the new broadcasting bill. The party directed its members to vote against it when introduced in parliament. The draft bill, which was referred to a sub-committee of the cabinet, apparently allowed foreign equity participation in satellite television and radio transmission. A senior CPM member said there was no question of any compromise regarding the provision. He indicated the party was not even ready to discuss the quantum or percentage of foreign equity, saying they were against any form of foreign participation.
RAYTHEON, OTHERS BAG $480 MLN SPIC PLANT

A consortium consisting of Raytheon Engineers and Constructors (REC), Singapore's Jurong Engineering, Deutsche Babock Energie and Umwelttechnik AG of Germany entered into a letter of intent for a 525 megawatt coal-fired power plant in Tamil Nadu. The plant would be built for Spic Electric Power Corporation (SEPC), a subsidiary of Southern Petrochemical Industries Corporation (SPIC). Total project cost was estimated at $480 million, of which Raytheon's share is valued at $210 million. REC will serve as project manager and provide engineering, procurement, commissioning, and testing services. LEHMAN BROS FORECASTS BULLISH TREND

Lehman Brothers predicted the Bombay bourse to touch 3,900 points in the next 12 months. In its latest research report, Lehman Brothers predicted a strong economic recovery and suggested investors move selectively away from stable sectors towards cyclicals such as cement and construction. The investment bank increased the weighting of Gujarat Ambuja Cement, Larsen & Toubro and Indian Hotels in its India model portfolio but decreased that of Hindustan Lever and state owned telecom firm MTNL. Business Line
ADDITIONAL 88 BLN RUPEE ANNUAL BURDEN

The fifth pay commission estimated the additional financial implications for one year would come to 88 billion rupees. But this figure would be reduced to 73 billion rupees for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) if savings, likely from postponement of retirement benefits was deducted. It further said arrears for the 15 months (January 1, 1996 to March 1997) were to be paid only for some of the items and the financial implication was likely to be 54.625 billion rupees. It suggested disbursing 50 percent of the arrears in cash and the balance to be deposited in the employees' general provident fund accounts.
